dominant_strengths: Clear hero hierarchy with serif/sans pairing communicates an editorial, considered tone for a productivity tool
Product screenshot is detailed and well-cropped, showing real UI density rather than abstract marketing fluff
Soft gradient backgrounds (blue hero, purple workflow band) create visual rhythm between sections
dominant_weaknesses: Top promo banner's saturated blue-to-purple gradient clashes with the softer pastel hero, fragmenting the palette
This is a marketing site, not a Mac app — native integration, motion, and system creativity can't really be judged from a landing page
Carousel arrows and dots feel generic; nothing about the layout is distinctive to Spark vs any SaaS template
fix_priorities: Unify the banner gradient with the hero tones so the page reads as one palette, not two stacked ads
Replace generic carousel chrome with a more bespoke navigation pattern that reflects email/AI metaphors
Tighten hero composition — the screenshot floats awkwardly right of an under-set headline column
Show actual macOS app chrome/behaviors if the brief is a Mac app, not just web marketing
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral gradients carry the page, behavioral signals are average web-CTA patterns, and reflective payoff is thin because nothing distinguishes Spark's worldview.
rationale.intent_fit: Weak fit: the brief asks for a Mac app design but this is a standard product landing page that only previews the app secondhand.
